key_facts: Lesions are symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions range from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
No hair growth at site of lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Stroma is formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on the face and neck, with a range of diameters from 2-3 mm to 25 mm, and the absence of hair growth in the affected areas, are consistent with the characteristics of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis. The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: Nevus depigmentosus typically presents as a single, well-defined hypopigmented patch, which does not match the multiple, symmetrically distributed lesions in this case.

rejected.label: Pityriasis alba
rejected.why: Pityriasis alba is a condition that typically affects children and is characterized by ill-defined, faintly hypopigmented patches with fine scaling, which does not match the well-defined, round macules in this case.

rejected.label: Vitiligo
rejected.why: Vitiligo is characterized by well-defined, depigmented patches due to the loss of melanocytes, which does not match the hypopigmented macules with preserved hair follicles and the specific histopathologic findings in this case.
